independent_review.review_scope: T103 factual read-only current review context and task-scoped paginated historical review UI; five product/test source files and existing related contract/authority code

deferred_minors.title: Application-completion fixture depends on Vue private event invoker storage
deferred_minors.behavior: trackReviewAction locates Symbol(_vei), replaces its click handler and awaits the original application promise. This gives stronger stale-response evidence than HTTP completion, but Vue can change this private event storage in a later upgrade.
deferred_minors.cost_if_wrong: A Vue refactor may break the fixture or make discovery fail before the product behavior is exercised. Current missing-handler and missing-Promise checks fail closed rather than falsely claim completion.
deferred_minors.disposition: Retain as nonblocking maintenance limitation for the pinned current Vue runtime; reassess when Vue or click-handler plumbing changes. Do not weaken completion or stale-result assertions.

root_rulings.finding: New UI sends only existing GET context and case_id/task_id-filtered history requests. It requires an authenticated user, review.read and visible case before read; server authority remains the actual object/source/policy boundary.
root_rulings.cost_if_wrong: Treating UI guards as authorization would overstate enforcement and could hide missing server checks.

root_rulings.finding: ReviewContext has no case_id field in the approved schema. Parent selects an actual queue row bound to the queried case, reader validates the task UUID, and existing server resource_scope binds the task and unit/case. No invented case field or public contract change is needed.
root_rulings.cost_if_wrong: Inventing or claiming a returned case_id would misdescribe the contract; client checks alone cannot prove authoritative case membership.

root_rulings.finding: Context and history are independent slots; each history record retains its own run/result/policy/review versions. Cross-run historical records are valid and are not overwritten by current context.
root_rulings.cost_if_wrong: Rejecting every historical version different from current would suppress valid review history; presenting current context as historical approval would misstate facts.

root_rulings.finding: Parent queue/selection and child reader observe generation, user, organization, role, permission and case membership changes; case edits, queue reload/page, task switch and unmount invalidate relevant results. Reader generations plus exact identity signature discard late successes and errors.
root_rulings.cost_if_wrong: Clearing the child alone would allow a previously displayed parent queue selection to re-open stale data.

root_rulings.boundary: Evidence and permissions are factual only
root_rulings.finding: The panel displays actual review decision and evidence identifiers, explicitly does not infer allowed actions, effective approval, validated evidence contents or download authority, and contains no new mutation.
root_rulings.cost_if_wrong: Treating a historical confirm_candidate or an evidence UUID as current approval or verified evidence could authorize an unsupported later action.

root_rulings.finding: New stale-response browser cases await the real returned Vue application promise after response release, including reader validation/catch/finally. They use owned transport fixtures and direct in-memory identity mutation, not real identity-provider or Linux backend end-to-end validation.
root_rulings.cost_if_wrong: HTTP-only waits can assert before stale errors reach application state; claiming real E2E from fixtures would inflate delivery evidence.

root_rulings.finding: This tranche is a read-only engineering substep. T103 forms, drafts, approved decisions, evidence reading and full real workflow remain separate. Root must independently bind final tests/CI/source hashes and GitHub/Linux sync; named owner/designated reviewer Xu Changsheng is not an actual human review result.
root_rulings.cost_if_wrong: Closing the whole task or inheriting another commit CI would overstate acceptance and conceal remaining work.
